rows.requirement_summary: Client transaction state machine behavior, timeouts, retries, aborts, and segmented response handling.
rows.notes: Clause 5.4.4.3 segmented ComplexACK admission stops RequestTimer after segment zero is saved. TSM-owned phase and activity-generation transitions serialize request retry authorization against admission without holding the TSM lock across transport I/O, and reject stale SegmentTimer expiry after new, duplicate, or out-of-order activity. Each registration also carries an immutable owner identity that qualifies request timer expiry, cancellation, receive-state activity/reset/completion, and dispatch-owned cleanup across immediate Invoke ID reuse. Clause 5.4.4.4 receive timeout uses four APDU segment timeouts, returns the local TSM_TIMEOUT ABORT.indication, promptly reclaims reassembly state without inbound traffic, and sends no peer PDU. The broader Clause 5.4.4 transition matrix still needs audit.

rows.requirement_summary: Server transaction state machine behavior, segmented request handling, routed peer correlation, SegmentACK behavior, and abort/reject mapping.
rows.notes: Server segmented transaction identity follows Clauses 5.3.5.3 and 6.2: valid routed SNET/SADR plus Invoke ID is stable across immediate routers, while local transactions use immediate MAC plus Invoke ID. Invalid routed metadata retains the immediate MAC and supplied metadata defensively. ConfirmedRequest reassembly, peer Abort removal, SegmentACK/Abort dispatch, and segmented ComplexACK sender registration use the same private key helper. Reply frames continue to use the current or captured immediate router MAC with NPDU DNET/DADR; the canonical empty-MAC sentinel is never a physical destination. Focused tests cover the identity matrix, routed request continuation and reply routing across routers, immediate peer-Abort cleanup, matching and mismatched routed sender events, and canonical sender replacement without stale cleanup. Existing send-side evidence remains: SegmentACKs with the server bit set are ignored; either ACK flavor naming the current segment advances; only a negative ACK naming the immediately preceding segment retransmits the current segment; stale and out-of-range ACKs are ignored; timeout, capacity, nonblocking dispatch, cancellation, and cleanup behavior remain covered. The row remains below supported status pending a fuller server TSM transition audit, configured APDU segment timeout/retry exposure, and broader Reject/Error failure mapping coverage.

rows.requirement_summary: Only Confirmed-Request and ComplexACK may be segmented; SegmentACK windows and modulo-256 sequence handling are enforced.
rows.notes: Receive-side client SEGMENTED_CONF and server SEGMENTED_REQUEST now use the Clause 5.4.2.2 predicate corrected by Addendum 135-2020ch, with modulo-256 unit vectors. Per-session DuplicateCount uses ActualWindowSize as Ndup: exactly Ndup in-window duplicates are discarded silently, the next is NAKed, and true out-of-order segments are NAKed immediately. Focused tests cover window one, windows greater than one, client/server baseline resets, ACK roles and fields, and byte-exact payload survival. The row remains below supported status pending multi-segment send-window behavior, full-transfer modulo-256 wrap evidence, max APDU/max segment boundaries, and broader TSM transition coverage.

rows.standard_anchor: Clauses 13.19-13.21; Clause 21.2.1, Clause 21.2.3, Clause 21.3.1, BACnetAuditNotification, BACnetAuditLogQueryParameters, and BACnetAuditOperationFlags productions
rows.requirement_summary: AuditNotification request payloads carry one or more typed BACnetAuditNotification values under context tag 0, while AuditLogQuery requests carry a typed by-target or by-source query alternative. The bundled server executes queries over explicitly persisted retained records and receives ConfirmedAuditNotification only through one explicit sink plus fail-closed transport-provenance authorization, bounded duplicate detection, and atomic durable merge-or-create. Within the primitive layer's u64 Unsigned domain, the codecs preserve the Clause 21 field order, tags, numeric domains, Boolean encoding, recipient alternatives, standard operation-flag bits 0-15, and proprietary bits 32-63; reject reserved flag bits, trailing or malformed structure; bound allocation; and leave destination buffers unchanged when validation fails.
rows.notes: Partial evidence for issue #345. The request/ACK models follow the Clause 21 field and tag productions within the library's u64 Unsigned implementation limit: start-at-sequence-number is Unsigned32 and successful-actions-only is BOOLEAN. Clause 13.19 instead describes Unsigned64 and the three-state BACnetSuccessFilter, including failures-only; that internal Standard conflict remains unresolved pending authoritative addendum or errata research, so this row stays below supported status. AuditLogQuery executes both alternatives over the explicitly persisted, already-loaded retained snapshot, traverses insertion order newest-first without numeric sorting, applies the literal Unsigned32 start predicate, scans completely for No_More_Items, and returns at most the 10,000-record persistence/ACK cap through the generic ComplexACK sizing and segmentation path. ConfirmedAuditNotification now decodes before policy/storage, requires one explicit Audit Log sink and a fail-closed fast authorizer, keeps immediate/routed transport provenance separate from peer-reported payload identity, and applies each accepted list in wire order through one prospective snapshot and durable commit. Complementary matching uses twice the configured Device APDU_Timeout as its window; like Time/DateTime variants compare temporal distance while SequenceNumber requires equality and mixed variants do not match. Exact pending/completed duplicates are silently discarded by a bounded 60-second, 256-entry process-local tracker; responses are not replayed and expiry/restart permits service again. Receiver payload/list caps of 64 KiB/256 are repository resource policy. Synchronous persistence under the database writer limits availability. Missing/non-Audit identifiers and absent query capability use the Clause 13.19 query errors; malformed payloads retain SERVICES/OTHER mapping. Raw target/current ANY values receive structural TLV validation only, not property-schema validation. Python exposes outbound Audit calls as byte escape hatches and no inbound builder. Unconfirmed AuditNotification, query authorization, sustained rate limiting, durable provenance/idempotency, failures-only queries, wrap-safe continuation, producer/forwarding policy, and Audit BIBB claims remain unsupported or deferred.

rows.requirement_summary: ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple, WriteProperty, and WritePropertyMultiple reject an array index supplied for a property that is not a BACnetARRAY with PROPERTY / PROPERTY_IS_NOT_AN_ARRAY, applying the per-object BACnetARRAY/BACnetLIST classification of Clause 12.1.5 (a BACnetLIST admits positional access only through ReadRange, Clause 12.1.5.2); true BACnetARRAY properties keep their index semantics.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#190, #260, #266). The gate is one query on the object (BACnetObject::is_array_property, default keyed by the Clause 12 object tables) so the classification cannot drift between services: identifier-stable BACnetARRAY properties modeled in-tree (OBJECT_LIST Table 12-13, PROPERTY_LIST, STATE_TEXT Tables 12-21/12-22/12-23, PRIORITY Table 12-24, WEEKLY_SCHEDULE/EXCEPTION_SCHEDULE Table 12-28, EVENT_TIME_STAMPS/EVENT_MESSAGE_TEXTS in the analog/binary/multi-state object tables, PRIORITY_ARRAY, TAGS Annex Y, SUBORDINATE_LIST/SUBORDINATE_ANNOTATIONS Table 12-34, GROUP_MEMBERS/GROUP_MEMBER_NAMES Table 12-57, ACTION Table 12-12, STAGES/STAGE_NAMES/TARGET_REFERENCES Table 12-80) admit an index; identifier-stable BACnetLIST properties (DATE_LIST Table 12-11, LIST_OF_GROUP_MEMBERS Table 12-17, RECIPIENT_LIST Table 12-24, LOG_BUFFER Tables 12-29/12-31, DEVICE_ADDRESS_BINDING and ACTIVE_COV_SUBSCRIPTIONS Table 12-13) and all scalars reject it; the type-dependent identifiers classify by object type (ALARM_VALUES/FAULT_VALUES array on CharacterString/BitString Value per Tables 12-44/12-47 but list on the multi-state/life-safety/access families, LIST_OF_OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCES array on Channel per Table 12-62 but list on Schedule/Timer per Tables 12-28/12-75, PRESENT_VALUE BACnetARRAY on Global Group per Table 12-57). Event_Time_Stamps and Event_Message_Texts implement the Clause 12.1.5.1 BACnetARRAY[3] read contract across all nine modeled intrinsic-reporting families: omitted index returns the ordered three transition slots, index 0 returns Unsigned(3), indexes 1..3 return one element, and larger indexes return PROPERTY / INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX. Event_Time_Stamps elements preserve the Clause 21 BACnetTimeStamp CHOICE and Clause 20.2 tag identities (Time [0], SequenceNumber [1], DateTime [2]) through object reads and RP/RPM encoding; Event_Message_Texts elements remain application-tagged CharacterString. EVENT_MESSAGE_TEXTS_CONFIG remains absent because no object-side model exists. Other array-typed identifiers whose object types are not modeled in-tree (ACTION_TEXT, VALUE_SOURCE_ARRAY, ...) stay rejected until their object-side modeling lands, so coverage is complete for the modeled set rather than for every array in the standard. The RP whitelist that admitted six always-list identifiers is gone; RPM gates per reference with inline error elements while siblings succeed; WP gates before decode/mutation; WPM gates in the validation phase so the commit loop never starts (mixed valid+gated requests commit nothing, proven by test). Indexed Recipient_List reads and writes fail with the same gate classification — mirrored at the object layer for direct calls — replacing the tranche-J INVALID_DATA_TYPE stopgap. #266: omitted-index (whole-array, Clause 12.1.5.1) Priority_Array writes are PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (a mappable Result(-)) while indexes 0 and 17 stay INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX; pinned at both macro sites and over the network WP/WPM paths. Limitations: the gate controls index admissibility only — object-side element semantics for Global Group / Channel / Structured View / Command / Staging arrays still return whole values, and CharacterString/BitString Value ALARM_VALUES/FAULT_VALUES are gate-classified as arrays but not yet modeled (an accepted index surfaces UNKNOWN_PROPERTY).

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 15.9.1.3 (WriteProperty error table) with Clause 21 BACnetNotifyType / BACnetEventTransitionBits / BACnetLimitEnable productions
rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty validation of the shared intrinsic-reporting event properties matches the Clause 15.9.1.3 error semantics: Notify_Type (BACnetNotifyType, a closed {alarm, event, ack-notification} production) refuses out-of-production values with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE ('The value provided is outside the range of values that the property can take on'), and Event_Enable / Limit_Enable (BACnetEventTransitionBits = 3 bits, BACnetLimitEnable = 2 bits) require the canonical encoding of their fixed-width production - exactly one content octet with 8-N declared unused bits, the form the read path emits - refusing any other shape with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING ('The encoding is not valid for the datatype of the property'). A previously-silent normalization of an over-long bit string (masking its first octet and dropping the declared count) is now a refusal, as is an empty content (previously INVALID_DATA_TYPE). Notify_Type membership derives from NotifyType::ALL_NAMED so a future addendum constant widens the gate without a second edit.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#255; behavior change - previously-accepted invalid writes now fail). The generic macro arms cover AI/AO/AV/BI/BO/BV/MSI/MSO/MSV, the analog macro arm adds Limit_Enable, and the EventEnrollment and AlertEnrollment objects carry their own arms with identical validation. A shared objects-layer helper (common::check_fixed_width_bit_string) shapes the PROPERTY-class error; the decoding-layer sibling in bacnet-encoding is intentionally not reused across layers. Covered shapes: out-of-production Notify_Type (3, 99, u32::MAX), an 8-bit string where the production defines fewer bits, extra or missing content octets, a half-octet string, and - for Limit_Enable - the valid Event_Enable 3-bit shape, which must not cross-apply. Related unaddressed family: the Notification Class recipient-list decoder still masks transition/day bit strings without consulting declared counts - noted as a follow-up rather than folded into this tranche.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 15.9 WriteProperty (15.9.1.2 Result(+), 15.9.1.3 Result(-)), Clause 15.10 WritePropertyMultiple, Clause 20.2.1 (concatenated elements)
rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple decode the entire propertyValue payload: elements are decoded with decode_application_value until the input is exhausted - the mirror of encode_property_value's List flattening - so one element yields the scalar PropertyValue and more than one yields PropertyValue::List. Full consumption is required: a partial or undecodable trailing element is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING per Clause 15.9.1.3 (The encoding is not valid for the datatype of the property) - never a silent drop - with the stored value proven unchanged; a well-formed extra element reaches a scalar arm and fails its shape as INVALID_DATA_TYPE. Empty payloads are also INVALID_DATA_ENCODING except for Fault_Signals, whose Clause 12.60 BACnetLIST may be empty and is delivered as PropertyValue::List. The RECIPIENT_LIST verbatim special-case keeps its precedence and the context-tagged ApplicationData widening of the single-element decoder is preserved (framed CHOICE properties, Clause 12.17 reference members).
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#182; behavior change - trailing bytes previously dropped between the single-element decoder and the arm now decide the write, and malformed value payloads map to PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING instead of the SERVICES/OTHER a propagated raw decoding error produced). A value TLV-truncated far enough to break framing is refused earlier by the service request's own [3]/[4] context walk (a framing error, still never silent; pinned by list_write_with_tlv_truncated_tail_is_refused_before_the_value_decode). WPM keeps its validate-all-then-commit-with-rollback semantics for structured values. Known residues (follow-ups, not regressions): AddListElement/RemoveListElement still break their listOfElements loop on an undecodable element instead of erroring (#182's wider scope); Enumerated contents wider than four octets still truncate to u32 (#277, explicitly untouched); and properties declared SEQUENCE OF beyond the four reference arms (e.g. LIST_OF_OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCES) keep their pre-existing arm-level behavior.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC BVLC-SC frame function, control, options, VMAC, and payload validation.
rows.notes: AB-01 adds transport codec evidence for Annex AB.2 control flag bits 7..4 rejection, Header Option Type 1..31 enforcement, AB.2.17 destination/data option marker decoding, VMAC field ordering, option count cap enforcement, option length truncation, option data truncation, and unterminated option-chain rejection. Received Encapsulated-NPDUs enforce Destination Option Must Understand semantics: an unsupported Must Understand option returns BVLC-Result NAK COMMUNICATION/HEADER_NOT_UNDERSTOOD for unicast, echoes the complete offending marker including More Options and an empty Header Data field, routes the Result to the source through the hub, and drops broadcast without a result. The hub applies its VMAC transformation while copying the validated option and payload bytes, avoiding marker normalization before the destination processes the frame. Must Understand clear does not block delivery. Addenda 135-2020cf/cp were checked for this row: cf renames Data Options bit 6 to Every Segment without changing the marker bit position, and cp adds standard header option types 2..5 that remain accepted by the generic 1..31 parser. Must Understand processing for other BVLC-SC functions, broader non-Result function-specific payload semantics, Every Segment segmentation behavior, and direct-connection behavior remain for later Annex AB work.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC BVLC-Result ACK/NAK payload parsing and connection handling.
rows.notes: AB-02 adds typed BVLC-Result ACK/NAK payload parsing for transport. ACK fixtures use the Proprietary-Message function per addendum 135-2020ci, while NAK fixtures mirror AB.2.17 examples with and without UTF-8 Error Details, including the Figure AB-6 multibyte UTF-8 details bytes. Negative evidence covers ACK trailing fields, short NAKs, unknown result codes, invalid UTF-8 details, malformed empty payloads, Data Options absence, Connect-Request NAK failing before timeout, fatal Result NAK closing the receive loop before further heartbeats, malformed wire-level Result decode failures closing without a Result response, and unicast Destination Option Must Understand failures returning COMMUNICATION/HEADER_NOT_UNDERSTOOD with the complete offending option marker. The hub relays a source-addressed, syntactically valid Encapsulated-NPDU Result to the originating node and drops peer Results for other functions so they cannot trigger the recipient's fatal Result handling. Transport connection handling keeps ACK and Encapsulated-NPDU NAK messages nonfatal, disconnects on other NAKs, and disconnects on malformed Result without generating a Result response. Negotiated Max-BVLC-Length resource-limit evidence is tracked under BACNET-AB-SC-CONNECTION-STATE. Remaining work includes request correlation for the permitted Encapsulated-NPDU Results, Error Details resource limits, standard-function ACK diagnostic policy, BVLC-Result generation for every AB.3.1.5 error situation, and direct-connection response routing.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC Data Options are exposed to the network layer as data_attributes and handled explicitly across supported SC/non-SC boundaries.
rows.notes: This row has native receive-side, outbound send, router local-delivery, and router forwarding evidence for BACnet/SC Encapsulated-NPDU Data Options. Receive paths convert every Data Option, including unknown options with bit 6 set, into generic transport DataAttribute values, preserving option type, the stored bit-6 flag, and option data on ReceivedNpdu; NetworkLayer exposes those attributes on ReceivedApdu after NPDU decode; router local-delivery paths retain inbound attributes; router forwarding attaches inbound attributes to forwarded unicast and broadcast SendRequest values; and non-SC transports emit empty data_attributes on receive. Native SC no longer applies Destination Option Must Understand rejection rules to Data Options. Destination Option rejection and BVLC-Result evidence is tracked under BACNET-AB-SC-FRAME and BACNET-AB-SC-BVLC-RESULT. Outbound paths add attribute-aware TransportPort and NetworkLayer send helpers, keep non-SC transports on default ignore-on-send behavior, and encode SC DataAttribute values as Data Options while validating option type 1..31, the 64-option cap, and u16 option-data lengths. Native negative tests enforce the Annex AB.2.3.1 Secure Path type-1 Must Understand and no-Header-Data marker constraints before message-ID allocation or BVLC-SC frame emission. Router tests cover forwarded unicast, forwarded broadcast, and loopback SC-to-SC forwarding preserving Data Options on the outbound SC frame. Remaining work includes Addendum 135-2020cf Every Segment semantics and a context-specific name for the stored Data Option bit-6 flag, high-level helper address-resolution/target-VMAC behavior, and formal conformance-test evidence.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC initiating and accepting peers enforce connection-state transitions, Connect-Accept response correlation, disconnect final-message behavior, and duplicate-VMAC collision signaling.
rows.notes: AB-03 adds native Connect-Accept message-id matching evidence, preserves the Connecting state when a pure state-machine response does not match the pending Connect-Request, and makes the async native handshake fail/disconnect on a mismatched response. Native Connect-Accept handling now requires the fixed AB.2.11.1 26-byte payload before entering Connected, stores peer Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length, advertises local Max-BVLC-Length, rejects outbound NPDUs or encoded BVLC frames that exceed peer limits, and discards oversized inbound WebSocket payloads before BVLC processing. The hub stores client Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length from Connect-Request, advertises its own limits in Connect-Accept, rejects non-26-byte Connect-Request payloads, drops inbound frames above the hub limit before decode, and filters unicast/broadcast relay targets by each recipient's negotiated NPDU and encoded BVLC limits. The hub BVLC-Result NAK builder now takes typed BACnet ErrorClass/ErrorCode values; duplicate client or hub VMAC collisions are encoded as COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151) instead of raw 1/1, and known-but-invalid functions are no longer classified as BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN. AB-07 stores each hub client's Device UUID, accepts known-UUID Connect-Request replacements, sends a WebSocket Close to the superseded connection, wakes the superseded handler, keeps superseded sinks from relaying or removing the replacement entry, and revalidates both source and recipient closed tokens immediately before relay writes so marked-superseded sinks are not written after replacement wins. It also preserves NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC NAK behavior for a new UUID that collides with an existing client or hub VMAC. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence now requires the superseded connection to receive a Close frame, rejects a second Connect-Request from an already connected client without replacing a peer that it claims, verifies the closed client's original VMAC is no longer reachable, verifies peer reachability after that invalid connected-state transition, and decodes duplicate-VMAC BVLC-Result NAK values at the WebSocket boundary. Transport receive-loop evidence now covers WebSocket close/error receive paths transitioning the native connection to Disconnected before exit, heartbeat send failures disconnecting before retry/exit, reconnect exhaustion leaving Disconnected, and oversized frame discard. Existing transport tests also cover connect timeout to Disconnected, Disconnect-Request construction, Disconnect-ACK transition from Disconnecting, and hub Device UUID payload parsing. This tranche adds Annex H.7.3 Random-48 VMAC generation, native Connect-Request BVLC-Result handling that detects COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151), requires the BVLC-Result message ID to match the pending Connect-Request before reseeding, disconnects, clears the pending connect, and installs a new Random-48 VMAC before later attempts. Native duplicate-VMAC reseed failure now blocks failover/retry eligibility so a stale duplicate VMAC is not sent on a subsequent failover Connect-Request. Failed primary-restore probes now copy a successful Random-48 reseed or fail-closed retry-block state back to the active connection before the probe is discarded, preventing later primary-restore or reconnect attempts from reusing a stale duplicate VMAC. Native connect-time failures now clear the pending Connect-Request on timeouts, invalid Connect-Accept responses, malformed BVLC-Result wires, generic SC decode errors, and WebSocket send/receive I/O errors. It also adds failover and primary-restore evidence that retry Connect-Requests use the reselected VMAC, primary-restore reseed-failure evidence that no stale-VMAC retry is sent, generic and wrong-message-id Connect-Request NAK evidence that does not reseed. Remaining AB.6.2 gaps include explicit AWAITING_WEBSOCKET modeling at the WebSocket adapter boundary, accepting-peer connect-wait timeout, Disconnect wait behavior in ScTransport::stop, and reserved VMAC error signaling.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC hub connector, hub relay behavior, VMAC routing, disconnect, and failover behavior are validated.
rows.notes: AB-06 adds hub connector/forwarding evidence for Annex AB.5.3.2, AB.5.3.3, and AB.5.4. Hub-bound Encapsulated-NPDU messages now carry Destination Virtual Address and omit Originating Virtual Address; local receive logic accepts hub-relayed unicast with no Destination Virtual Address and drops non-broadcast Destination Virtual Address from hub relay. The hub rejects forwarding attempts with an Originating Virtual Address or missing Destination Virtual Address, selects only the matching VMAC for unicast, discards unknown unicast destinations by producing no recipient, fans broadcast to all current hub connections except the origin, preserves Message ID/payload/destination options/data options, adds the sender Originating Virtual Address, strips Destination Virtual Address for unicast forwarding, and preserves broadcast Destination Virtual Address for broadcast forwarding. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence covers three connected clients: A-to-B unicast reaches only B with the required VMAC transformation and option preservation, A-to-unknown unicast reaches no client, and A broadcast reaches B and C but not A while preserving the broadcast Destination Virtual Address. AB-07 adds live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that a known Device UUID replacement moves hub reachability to the replacement VMAC, prevents old-VMAC unicast delivery, requires a Close frame for the superseded connection, prevents marked-superseded source or recipient sinks from relaying after replacement wins, and preserves peer reachability after rejecting a connected client's second Connect-Request. Transport connector evidence now covers initial primary timeout to failover, established primary loss with reconnect exhaustion, failover Connect-Request/Connect-Accept, connection state update, active unicast send-path swap to the failover hub, and primary restoration while failover is active. Primary restoration uses a separate probe connection, sends a best-effort Disconnect-Request to the failover hub after the primary Connect-Accept succeeds, swaps the active transport path back to the primary hub, and verifies subsequent unicast traffic is sent to the restored primary. This slice adds relay helper and live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that 31 minimum-size Destination Options plus 31 minimum-size Data Options remain within the 1476-byte BVLC size budget and are preserved through hub unicast relay; helper coverage also verifies broadcast preservation with the same option chains. This slice also adds explicit unsupported direct-connection classification evidence: the hub WebSocket subprotocol selection rejects `dc.bsc.bacnet.org`, and a connected hub client sending Address-Resolution receives a BVLC-Result NAK with COMMUNICATION/UNEXPECTED_DATA rather than BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN. Configured hub URI evidence covers the production TlsWebSocket::connect parse boundary preserving the configured wss authority, port, path, and query before dialing; malformed or hostless configured hub URIs are rejected before any WebSocket/TLS dial. ASHRAE Addendum cc to 135-2020 changes AB.5.3.1 hub-connection metadata and Network Port properties but does not change these forwarding, replacement, reconnect-failover, option-preservation, configured/malformed hub URI, or direct-connection unsupported-classification behaviors. rows.requirement_summary: The Event Enrollment evaluator honors both delays and executes transition actions for every indicated transition. pTimeDelay (Event_Parameters.Time_Delay per Table 12-15) gates transitions into OFFNORMAL states; pTimeDelayNormal - the EE object's new optional Time_Delay_Normal property (Unsigned, Table 12-14 O, writable under the Clause 12.1.2 option, read-back falling back to Time_Delay per Clause 13.3: 'if no value is available for this parameter, then it takes on the value of the pTimeDelay parameter') - gates transitions to NORMAL. The pending countdown is owned by the EE object in-memory behind a guarded internal trait channel (mirroring set_event_state_internal, #130) and advances once per evaluation pass of the event_enrollment_task interval (#133): condition-revert cancels, a redundant qualifying observation never re-seeds (Clause 13.2.4 debounce), a changed target re-seeds with the new target's direction delay, and a parameter change mid-pending (parameters and the effective TDN are fingerprinted per pass) cancels and re-gates. Per Clause 13.2.2.1.4 the actions run 'even if the transition does not change the event state': the SPECIFIC returned state is stored ('it is not acceptable to set Event_State to OFFNORMAL when the returned value is HIGH_LIMIT'), the Acked_Transitions bit is maintained per Clause 13.2.3 (cleared when the referenced Notification Class's Ack_Required marks the transition ack-owed, otherwise set; an unresolvable class is not-required), and the transition is emitted with its Event_Enable-scoped distribute flag (Clause 12.12 / 13.2.5). Committed Event Enrollment results select their model EventType through the shared EventStateChange selector: FAULT entry, changed-Reliability FAULT re-entry, and recovery select CHANGE_OF_RELIABILITY, while non-FAULT transitions retain the configured algorithm. This slice does not route or emit Event Notifications; that remains #127 / PR-0305. CHANGE_OF_STATE condition (c) (Optional:) is implemented via the retained last-offnormal-causing value so OFFNORMAL->OFFNORMAL re-indicates; CHANGE_OF_BITSTRING condition (c) (Optional:) is deliberately unimplemented and documented. CHANGE_OF_VALUE tracks the Clause 13.3.3 detection baseline (the value at the last indicated NORMAL transition): both criteria compare against it (REAL: |current - baseline| >= a positive pIncrement; BIT STRING: significant masked-bit change), the only indication is NORMAL->NORMAL (Figure 13-10), the baseline advances at each indicated NORMAL transition, and the first observed sample initializes the baseline without indicating (the clause's explicit local matter).

rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (issues #163 delay honoring, #166 same-state transition actions, #137 COV baseline; branch codex/ee-evaluator-delays, tranche C2). Extract verification: Time_Delay_Normal's Table 12-14 row read in the two-column interleave as name/type/conformance triples adjacent to Event_Algorithm_Inhibit O1 and Status_Flags R (16444-16446), its property text quoted at 16887-16889, and Table 12-15's per-algorithm Time_Delay -> pTimeDelay mapping confirmed for all five evaluated algorithms (16530-16679); 13.2.2.1.4 and 13.2.3 quoted verbatim. Tick semantics: Clause 13.3's delays are seconds ('the time, in seconds, that the offnormal conditions must exist') and are honored in wall time: the countdown is seeded with ceil(delay_secs / interval_secs) - never-fire-early ceiling semantics against the actual (>=1s-clamped) event_enrollment_interval_secs (#133), so at the 10s default a 5s delay fires on the ~10s tick, a 15s delay on the ~20s tick, a 25s delay on the ~30s tick, all pinned by start_paused lifecycle tests - and decrements once per evaluation pass. The interval is builder configuration and the countdown is in-memory, so no runtime rescale exists; a restart re-evaluates with a fresh conversion (the per-pass misreading this supersedes was issue #163's original suggested direction, caught in the PR-#290 review). Ownership: the pending countdown, the COS last-offnormal value, and the COV baseline live in the EE object (in-memory only, matching the intrinsic detectors' restart semantics) instead of evaluator-side maps, so they survive evaluation cycles and stay object-owned behind guards that refuse writes while detection is disabled; the Clause 13.2.2.1 detection-disabled reset clears all three. Struct discipline: the EE pending type does NOT reuse the intrinsic PendingTransition - the mechanisms are structurally similar but do not share code across the objects/server boundary (per-cycle vs probe/tick cadence) - and the condition identity additionally discriminates by matched alarm value (COS) or masked monitored bytes (COBS), stricter than the intrinsic detectors' target-only identity. Fences honored: no notification emission (#127, tranche E - the lifecycle task still only logs), no Event_Time_Stamps/Event_Message_Texts on the EE object (tranche E, #264), no Status_Flags algorithm input (Table 12-15.1) - CHANGE_OF_STATE/COBS conditions here take pStatusFlags as all-FALSE per the standard's own absent-parameter fallback; flagged as tranche-E follow-up. No intrinsic-detector changes. Deliberately-remained gaps: CHANGE_OF_BITSTRING condition (c) (Optional:, no bitstring baseline retained); OUT_OF_RANGE 13.3.6 (c)/(f) no-delay returns when a limit is disabled (also deferred by BACNET-12-TIME-DELAY-NORMAL); fault-precedence for EE (the evaluator evaluates no reliability term) unchanged and out of scope. Behavior-change note: two pre-#137 COV tests pinned absolute-magnitude OFFNORMAL indications the standard's Figure 13-10 cannot produce; they were rewritten to the conformant baseline semantics. Custom downstream EE-typed objects that skip the new internal channel degrade fail-closed: evaluation runs, TD=0 transitions fire as before, but nonzero delays never fire and COV never indicates (documented in the trait docs). PR-#290 review round (runtime+adversary+dataflow lanes): (B1) the countdown originally counted evaluation PASSES while Clause 13.3's delays are seconds - fixed by threading the actual interval in (evaluate_event_enrollments now takes interval_secs; lifecycle passes the clamped period) and seeding remaining = ceil(delay_secs / interval_secs), never-fire-early ceiling semantics; residual behavior documented (builder-config interval + in-memory pending => no runtime rescale; restart re-evaluates with a fresh conversion). (B2) foreign Event_State wedge: params rewritten to a different algorithm left states the new arm's conditions never name, and the keyed conditions matched nothing forever - each arm now names its reachable set (OOR/FL {NORMAL,HIGH_LIMIT,LOW_LIMIT}; COS/COBS {NORMAL,OFFNORMAL}; COV {NORMAL}) and, outside it, evaluates as from NORMAL and indicates the computed state through the ordinary actions path (delay-gated; COV's recovery installs the sample as the 13.3.3 baseline). (B3) AcknowledgeAlarm on EE previously failed via the trait default - EventEnrollmentObject now implements the 13.2.3 acknowledgment indication (unconditional idempotent set), refusing OBJECT/NO_ALARM_CONFIGURED per Table 13-10 while detection is disabled; OOS does not gate ack. (F4) the fingerprint-cancellation is flushed before any later exit (an A->B->A params round-trip can no longer resume a stale countdown; the unreadable-reference exit deliberately precedes the check). (F5) monitored object+property folded into params_fingerprint. (F2) structured COBS matcher compares over max(mask,value) with zero-filled bytes (was min-width truncation: false OFFNORMAL on prefix match). (N2) pending value-identity strictness re-anchored on 13.3.2 (c)'s 'remains equal to THAT value' with (a)'s 'ANY of the values' called out as the stricter deliberate choice. Added while in the file: TO_NORMAL ack-required coverage and the Event_Enable-vs-ack independence pin. Out of scope per the review: #179 (EE Status_Flags IN_ALARM) stays tranche E. PR-0303 policy gate (#305/D4; repository-local policy, not a normative BACnet requirement): any valid but unavailable monitored observation clears pending delay, the COV baseline, last-offnormal carryover, and monitored-source ownership; restoration or retargeting requires a fresh baseline and the full applicable delay. Invalid configuration remains on the PR-0302 CONFIGURATION_ERROR path. A transient gap remains ObservationUnavailable and causes no Reliability, Event_State, Acked_Transitions, event-history, or timestamp transition. Implementation evidence is `crates/bacnet-server/src/event_enrollment/{mod.rs,support.rs,commit.rs}`; exact executable coverage is recorded in this row's PR-0303 continuity and legacy-report test entries.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.13 (Table 12-16 File_Access_Method), Clauses 14.1 and 14.2 (Incorrect File access method), Clauses 14.1.4.1 and 14.2.4.1 (non-File Object Identifier), Clause 14.2.4.1 (Write to a read-only File), Clause 18 (INVALID_FILE_ACCESS_METHOD, FILE_ACCESS_DENIED, and INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_TYPE), Clause 21 (BACnetFileAccessMethod production; AtomicReadFile/AtomicWriteFile access-method CHOICE)
rows.requirement_summary: The bundled server cross-checks each AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile request's access method against the target File object's declared File_Access_Method before any ACK is encoded or object state is mutated. The request CHOICE maps semantically to the property enumeration (stream request -> STREAM_ACCESS, record request -> RECORD_ACCESS), never by CHOICE tag number (stream is CHOICE [0] but enumeration value 1; record is CHOICE [1] but enumeration value 0). A mismatch, an unreadable property, a wrong property datatype, or an out-of-production raw value fails closed with SERVICES / INVALID_FILE_ACCESS_METHOD for a File object that exposes storage; a File-typed object without storage is refused SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED directly after the lookup (see BACNET-14-FILE-STORAGE). AtomicWriteFile refuses a matching-method File whose Read_Only property is TRUE before access-method validation, mutation, or ACK encoding with SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED. Both services classify a non-File object identifier as SERVICES / INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_TYPE before the object lookup, so an absent non-File identifier is classified by its type while a missing File object remains OBJECT / UNKNOWN_OBJECT. This row covers only access-method cross-checking, non-File identifier classification, and the read-only AtomicWriteFile refusal; no broader File service support (stream/record storage completeness, append semantics, ReadRange) is claimed.
rows.notes: Narrow row added with #287. The four-way mismatch matrix pins the exact SERVICES / INVALID_FILE_ACCESS_METHOD pairing, response-buffer atomicity, and no-mutation on refused writes. Matching-method stream and record tests pin the Clause 14.2.4.1 SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED read-only refusal, byte-identical sentinel response buffers, and unchanged FILE_SIZE and RECORD_COUNT state. Storage behaviour (stream/record persistence, append, start-position validation, growth cap) is covered by BACNET-14-FILE-STORAGE (#397). Non-File identifier tests (#398) pin SERVICES / INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_TYPE for both present and absent non-File identifiers, OBJECT / UNKNOWN_OBJECT for a missing File object, byte-identical sentinel response buffers, and unchanged read-only precedence for File identifiers. The standard does not sequence the non-File type check against the existence check, so classifying an absent non-File identifier by type is a deliberate choice recorded with #398.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.13 / Table 12-16 (File object property model; no File Data property; File_Size and Record_Count), Clause 14.1 (AtomicReadFile parameters, End Of File, Service Procedure), Clause 14.2 (AtomicWriteFile parameters, -1 append, Service Procedure, Result(+) position), Clauses 14.1.4.1 and 14.2.4.1 (INVALID_FILE_START_POSITION), Clause 14.2.4.1 (FILE_FULL), Clause 18 (INVALID_FILE_START_POSITION, FILE_FULL, FILE_ACCESS_DENIED), Annex F (AtomicWriteFile append example)
rows.requirement_summary: The bundled server's AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile service handlers reach a File object's contents through the internal FileStorage channel exposed by the BACnetObject file_storage_internal hooks, never through a property. Stream and record reads return the stored octets and records for the requested window, short reads return what remains, and End Of File is TRUE only when the returned window includes the last octet or record (Clause 14.1.3.1: "TRUE if this response includes the last octet of the file and FALSE otherwise"), so an empty window at the end reports FALSE. Stream and record writes persist, extend the file when the start is past its end (zero octets and empty records as the local-matter fill), keep File_Size and Record_Count coherent, honour -1 as append, and acknowledge the position actually written. A read start that is negative or past the end, or a write start that is negative other than -1, is refused SERVICES / INVALID_FILE_START_POSITION; a write that would grow the file past the object's designed limit (1 MiB of octets and 10,000 records by default, the record cap being the workspace decoder's own SEQUENCE OF ceiling so a read-back at the cap stays decodable) is refused OBJECT / FILE_FULL; a File-typed object without storage is refused SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED directly after the lookup, as is a write to a File whose Read_Only is TRUE, unreadable, or not a BOOLEAN (the gate fails closed); a record write whose payload list is shorter than its Record Count is rejected MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMETER. Every refusal the handlers raise leaves the object and the response buffer unchanged; a FileStorage implementation that returns a write position outside the ACK's INTEGER range can leave the object mutated and still draw DEVICE / INTERNAL_ERROR. A record read returns at most MAX_DECODED_ITEMS (10,000) records in one ACK, the workspace decoder's SEQUENCE OF ceiling; a larger file reads back in windows, with Returned Record Count below the request and End Of File FALSE until the last window. This row covers only the storage path behind the BACNET-14-FILE-ACCESS-METHOD gates; no broader File service support (Modification_Date/Archive maintenance, File_Size/Record_Count writability, ReadRange) is claimed.
rows.notes: Row added with #397. Gate order: object type, then lookup, then storage presence (the Clause 14.1 / 14.2 Service Procedures decide "currently inaccessible for another reason" in their first step), then read-only (writes, failing closed on an unreadable property), then access method (unchanged from #287/#398/#399), and only then the storage channel's start-position and capacity checks. End Of File follows the letter of Clause 14.1.3.1 and the Service Procedure: an empty window, including a read whose start equals the file size or a zero count, reports FALSE. The growth caps (1 MiB of octets, 10,000 records by default, per object, growth-only so preloaded contents past the cap are still overwritten in place — pinned by tests whose in-place windows cross the cap) are the designed limit Clause 18 defines FILE_FULL for; the caps are not BACnet properties and never appear in Property_List. AtomicWriteFile record decoding requires the file-record-data cardinality to equal Record Count (#418), matching Clause 14.2's specified number of records: a short list is rejected MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMETER, and an extra element inside context [1] is rejected TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS. The handler retains its count/vector check as defense in depth before lookup or mutation. The handler's access-method gate is pinned independently of FileObject's own check with a lax custom storage; FileStorage's defaulted methods report FILE_ACCESS_DENIED (no implementation behind them), never a method mismatch. Deferred, with the spec text that governs them: Modification_Date update and Archive reset on a write (Clause 12.13, Modification_Date condition (b) and Archive); File_Size and Record_Count writability with truncate/expand semantics (Table 12-16 footnotes 1 and 2); locking beyond the object-database guard the dispatcher already holds for the whole handler; a Python binding for preloading or reading file contents. The read handler clamps a record window to MAX_DECODED_ITEMS so one ACK never exceeds what the workspace decoder accepts, which also covers files preloaded past the record cap through set_records. This is a recorded departure from the Clause 14.1 Service Procedure, which short-reads only when fewer records remain; the clamp adds a second, local reason. Clause 14.1.3.1 makes End Of File a data-independent end-of-file test, so a client that continues from start + Returned Record Count still reads the whole file. FileObject::set_data and set_records update File_Size and Record_Count only for the channel File_Access_Method selects (any value other than RECORD_ACCESS is the stream channel) and set_file_access_method recomputes both on a switch, so Record_Count is present only under RECORD_ACCESS (Table 12-16 footnote 2).
